articles.title: Ares Provides $2 Billion Debt Facility To Phoenix Tower International As Part Of $6.5 Billion Financing
articles.snippet:
Ares Management provided $2 billion of a $6.5 billion multi-jurisdiction financing for Phoenix Tower International. Ares funded approximately $1.8 billion at closing.
The post Ares Provides $2 Billion Debt Facility To Phoenix Tower International As Part Of $6.5 Billion Financing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Ares Provides $2 Billion Debt Facility To Phoenix Tower International As Part Of $6.5 Billion Financing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Ares Provides $2 Billion Debt Facility To Phoenix Tower International As Part Of $6.5 Billion Financing
Ares Management provided $2 billion of a $6.5 billion multi-jurisdiction financing for Phoenix Tower International. Ares funded approximately $1.8 billion at closing.
The financing represents one of the largest private credit transactions completed to date in the telecommunications tower sector.
Phoenix Tower International plans to use the new debt facility to consolidate existing loans and create additional capacity to fund expansion in existing and new international markets.
PTI owns and operates more than 33,000 wireless sites across 23 countries.
Ares Infrastructure Debt played a significant role in structuring the financing.
The strategy provides capital to infrastructure businesses operating across digital infrastructure, power, midstream, transportation, and utilities.
Ares Infrastructure managed approximately $29.9 billion in assets as of June 30, 2026 and had more than 130 investment professionals globally.
PTI described the broader $6.5 billion financing as the largest transaction of its kind for a privately held tower company.
The financing strengthens PTI’s capital structure while providing additional resources for continued global expansion.
Ares Management managed more than $671 billion of assets across its broader global investment platform as of June 30, 2026.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased to deepen our longstanding partnership with PTI through this landmark financing.”
“PTI has established itself as one of the premier independent telecommunications tower platforms globally, with a differentiated portfolio of high-quality assets, an exceptional management team and a proven track record of disciplined growth across diverse markets.”
Roopa Murthy, Partner and Co-Head of EMEA Infrastructure Debt at Ares
“This $6.5 billion financing, the largest of its kind for a privately held tower company, reflects our lenders’ confidence in PTI and our team’s execution across 23 jurisdictions.”
Michael Bremer, CFO of Phoenix Tower International

articles.title: Axiom Secures $2 Billion Convertible Preferred Investment At $37.5 Billion Enterprise Value
articles.snippet:
Axiom Solutions International has secured a $2 billion convertible preferred equity investment led by General Catalyst and Koch Equity Development, along with co-investors, at an initial enterprise value of $37.5 billion.
The post Axiom Secures $2 Billion Convertible Preferred Investment At $37.5 Billion Enterprise Value appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Axiom Secures $2 Billion Convertible Preferred Investment At $37.5 Billion Enterprise Value
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Axiom Secures $2 Billion Convertible Preferred Investment At $37.5 Billion Enterprise Value
Axiom Solutions International has secured a $2 billion convertible preferred equity investment led by General Catalyst and Koch Equity Development, along with co-investors, at an initial enterprise value of $37.5 billion.
Axiom is currently Flex’s Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment and is expected to be separated into an independent publicly traded company during the first quarter of 2027.
Funds affiliated with General Catalyst, Koch Equity Development and participating co-investors agreed to purchase $2 billion of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock in Axiom.
On a pro forma basis following the separation, the investment will be entirely in Axiom.
The proceeds are expected to help finance Axiom’s previously announced acquisition of EPC Power and provide the company with additional balance-sheet capacity as it prepares to become independent.
Net proceeds can be used to fund part of the EPC Power purchase price, repay equity bridge or other intermediate financing related to that acquisition, pay dividends on the preferred stock or support general corporate purposes.
Flex separately secured committed term-loan financing for the remaining portion of the EPC Power transaction.
The preferred stock will initially pay a 10% annual cash dividend before the separation.
Following the separation, the dividend will step down to 6% annually if paid in cash or 7% if paid in kind, subject to potential increases after the fifth anniversary of the separation and other adjustments.
General Catalyst will also receive the right to nominate one director to Axiom’s board after the separation is completed.
The investment remains subject to customary regulatory approvals and closing conditions.
Flex expects Axiom to focus on power, thermal and compute infrastructure supporting growing artificial intelligence infrastructure demand.
PJT Partners is serving as financial adviser and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom is providing legal counsel to Flex.
Davis Polk & Wardwell is serving as legal counsel to General Catalyst.
KEY QUOTES:
“This investment provides equity funding for our recently announced acquisition of EPC Power and will allow Axiom to have a strong balance sheet as we prepare to stand up as an independent, publicly traded company squarely focused on the power, thermal, and compute infrastructure the AI era demands. General Catalyst brings deep conviction in applied AI and a long track record partnering with companies building category-defining leaders, and we’re glad to have them partner with us as Axiom enters its next chapter. This transaction reflects the value we see in Axiom’s business today and will translate into lasting value for Flex shareholders as the separation comes together.”
Revathi Advaithi, Chief Executive Officer of Flex and Expected Chief Executive Officer of Axiom
“Axiom sits at the center of the power and infrastructure buildout that AI demands, and we’ve been impressed by the team’s execution and the scale of the opportunity ahead. We look forward to partnering with Axiom for the long term as it becomes an independent company and continues to invest in the technology and capacity this next phase of growth requires.”
Hemant Taneja, Chief Executive Officer of General Catalyst

articles.title: Oaktree Asset-Backed Finance Fund Closes At $2 Billion
articles.snippet:
Oaktree has closed its Asset-Backed Finance Fund (ABF I) with $2 billion in commitments across the fund and related investment vehicles. The final close reached the fund's fundraising target and attracted a globally diversified group of institutional investors.
The post Oaktree Asset-Backed Finance Fund Closes At $2 Billion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Oaktree Asset-Backed Finance Fund Closes At $2 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
Oaktree Asset-Backed Finance Fund Closes At $2 Billion
Oaktree has closed its Asset-Backed Finance Fund (ABF I) with $2 billion in commitments across the fund and related investment vehicles. The final close reached the fund’s fundraising target and attracted a globally diversified group of institutional investors.
Investors included U.S. public pension plans and sovereign wealth funds, reflecting growing institutional interest in private asset-backed finance strategies.
The close is in addition to Oaktree’s separate asset-backed vehicle focused on private wealth investors.
Oaktree’s strategy provides flexible capital to originators across areas including equipment leasing, transportation, consumer finance, real estate and infrastructure.
The firm has been investing in asset-backed finance for more than two decades.
Across its broader asset-backed finance platform, Oaktree has invested more than $19 billion and developed relationships with hundreds of third-party originators.
ABF I also builds on Brookfield’s partnership with Oaktree, which dates to 2019.
The strategy now uses Brookfield’s global operating platform to support sourcing, underwriting and investment analysis across the asset-backed finance market.
Brookfield’s broader asset-based finance platform totals more than $60 billion.
Its investment areas include specialty finance, residential non-qualified mortgages, aviation lending, music royalties, fund finance and digital infrastructure leases.
Oaktree operates as part of Brookfield’s $416 billion credit platform.
KEY QUOTE:
“As the private asset-backed market grows, its sheer variety across sectors, structures and risk/return makes the market difficult to navigate. We see that as opportunity, giving us real freedom to pursue the best relative value. Our approach is simple: survey a very broad market for less-crowded lending opportunities, and subject them to Oaktree’s critical eye. The partnership with Brookfield has supercharged our proprietary sourcing and added differentiated perspectives to our investment decisions.”
Brendan Beer, Managing Director and Portfolio Manager at Oaktree

articles.title: Biohub, DOE, NIH And Partners Commit $1.8 Billion To Build AI-Ready Biology Data
articles.snippet:
Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health and private-sector partners have announced a coordinated $1.8 billion commitment of funding, data, computing resources and measurement technology to create foundational biological data for predictive AI models.
The post Biohub, DOE, NIH And Partners Commit $1.8 Billion To Build AI-Ready Biology Data appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Biohub, DOE, NIH And Partners Commit $1.8 Billion To Build AI-Ready Biology Data
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Biohub, DOE, NIH And Partners Commit $1.8 Billion To Build AI-Ready Biology Data
Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health and private-sector partners have announced a coordinated $1.8 billion commitment of funding, data, computing resources and measurement technology to create foundational biological data for predictive AI models.
The initiative is intended to build an open resource that researchers can use to develop AI systems capable of predicting how biological systems and human cells respond to interventions.
The Department of Energy plans to invest more than $500 million over five years in laboratory measurement, modeling and computation.
NIH will coordinate datasets, repositories and knowledge bases generated through more than $500 million of previous federal investment, with Biohub working to standardize that information for AI model training.
Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta are collectively investing another $300 million in the Virtual Biology Initiative.
Biohub previously committed $500 million to the initiative, including $400 million for technologies such as cryo-electron tomography, advanced microscopy and biological engineering tools, plus $100 million for external research.
The broader effort aims to provide the data required to develop virtual biological models that could allow researchers to conduct portions of experiments digitally before moving into physical laboratories.
DOE will contribute through its Genesis Mission, drawing on resources including exascale supercomputers, X-ray and neutron scattering, cryo-electron microscopy and autonomous laboratories across the National Laboratory system.
NIH will contribute through its Bio Genesis Mission and existing biomedical repositories and research programs.
Other participating scientific organizations include the Allen Institute, Broad Institute, Gladstone Institutes, Human Cell Atlas, Human Protein Atlas and Wellcome Sanger Institute.
NVIDIA will contribute accelerated computing infrastructure, software and technical expertise, while Renaissance Philanthropy is helping expand funding for data generation.
KEY QUOTES:
“An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally. The insights that come from this could unlock a far greater understanding of disease and open up completely new paths for cures. Because of this potential, the creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together. We invite the worldwide scientific community to join us in this project.”
Alex Rives, Head of Science at Biohub
“Generating the data to solve predictive systems biology requires scaling past the limits of what any single organization can produce today. By joining the Virtual Biology Initiative as a founding member, Isomorphic Labs is helping build a massive, multimodal data foundation. This initiative will generate the data needed to push the industry closer to the next significant breakthrough for biology.”
Max Jaderberg, President of Isomorphic Labs

articles.title: BBAM Closes Incline Aviation III At More Than $1.7 Billion
articles.snippet:
BBAM has completed the final close of Incline Aviation III with more than $1.7 billion in total capital commitments, marking the third flagship aviation fund in the investment manager’s Incline platform. The fund received commitments from a mix of existing and new institutional investors.
The post BBAM Closes Incline Aviation III At More Than $1.7 Billion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
BBAM Closes Incline Aviation III At More Than $1.7 Billion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
BBAM Closes Incline Aviation III At More Than $1.7 Billion
BBAM has completed the final close of Incline Aviation III with more than $1.7 billion in total capital commitments, marking the third flagship aviation fund in the investment manager’s Incline platform. The fund received commitments from a mix of existing and new institutional investors.
Incline Aviation III will continue the investment strategy established by its predecessor funds, targeting opportunities throughout the commercial aviation market. Its investment mandate includes aircraft, engines and aviation-related credit opportunities.
The latest fund represents an increase in size compared with the previous generations of the strategy. Incline Aviation I raised $1.2 billion of commitments including affiliated co-investment, while Incline Aviation II secured $1.5 billion. BBAM brings nearly four decades of experience sourcing, acquiring, financing, and managing commercial aircraft globally.
Incline Aviation III has already begun deploying its capital. As of June 2026, investors had invested or committed more than $625 million in equity, representing about 37% of the final fund size.
BBAM is one of the world’s largest aircraft lessors, providing fleet and financing solutions to more than 100 airline customers across more than 50 countries. The firm has more than 500 aircraft under management and employs more than 150 aviation professionals across offices in Dallas, Dublin, Puerto Rico, San Francisco, Seoul, Singapore, Tokyo and Zurich. KEY QUOTES:
“We appreciate the confidence that both existing and new investors have placed in BBAM through Incline Aviation III. Our focus remains on deploying capital selectively into opportunities where our experience, scale and global aviation relationships can create meaningful value.”
Steve Zissis, President And Chief Executive Officer Of BBAM

articles.title: Lamb Weston: Q1 Revenue Rises To $1.67 Billion As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
articles.snippet:
Lamb Weston reported fiscal 2027 first-quarter net sales of $1.67 billion, up 1% from $1.66 billion in the prior-year period and above the company's expectations.
The post Lamb Weston: Q1 Revenue Rises To $1.67 Billion As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Lamb Weston: Q1 Revenue Rises To $1.67 Billion As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Lamb Weston: Q1 Revenue Rises To $1.67 Billion As Company Raises Fiscal 2027 Outlook
Lamb Weston reported fiscal 2027 first-quarter net sales of $1.67 billion, up 1% from $1.66 billion in the prior-year period and above the company’s expectations.
Sales volume increased 2%, while price and mix declined 2%.
Net income totaled $29 million compared with $64 million a year earlier.
Adjusted net income was $103 million, unchanged from the prior-year period.
Diluted earnings per share declined to $0.21 from $0.46, while adjusted diluted EPS increased to $0.75 from $0.74.
Adjusted EBITDA totaled $286 million compared with $302 million a year earlier.
North America remained the company’s strongest-performing segment.
North America net sales increased 5% to $1.14 billion as sales volume grew 7%, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of volume growth.
North America adjusted EBITDA increased 11% to $287 million.
The gains reflected higher volumes, cost-saving initiatives, tariff refunds, and increased equity-method investment earnings.
International revenue declined 8% to $529 million.
International adjusted EBITDA declined 54% to $27 million as lower European sales volumes, higher manufacturing costs, factory underutilization, inflation, and prior-year potato crop costs pressured results.
Lamb Weston said capacity optimization efforts in North America have increased utilization by approximately 10 percentage points.
The company also ended production at its Broekhuizenvorst facility and transitioned customer fulfillment elsewhere in its network to improve international utilization and costs.
Operating cash flow totaled $235 million during the quarter.
Capital expenditures were $91 million.
Lamb Weston ended the quarter with $166 million in cash and cash equivalents and another $1.24 billion of available liquidity under its revolving credit facility.
The company returned $52 million to shareholders through dividends during the quarter.
Its board subsequently declared another quarterly dividend of $0.38 per share.
Following the better-than-expected first quarter, Lamb Weston increased several fiscal 2027 targets.
The company now expects net sales to increase at a low-single-digit rate compared with its previous forecast of flat to 1% growth.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance increased to between $1.125 billion and $1.215 billion from $1.10 billion to $1.20 billion.
Adjusted diluted EPS guidance increased to $3.05 to $3.35 from $2.95 to $3.25.
Lamb Weston continues to expect between $750 million and $800 million of operating cash flow during fiscal 2027.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are off to a solid start to the year, delivering first quarter net sales and profit above our expectations.”
“Our first quarter results were driven by continued momentum in North America where our strong customer relationships fueled sales volume growth and we continued to drive cost savings.”
“We continue to experience unexpected inflationary pressure across key input costs and freight expense. Our teams are addressing cost inflation by working with suppliers and hedging where possible.”
“At the same time, we continue to make meaningful progress advancing our Focus to Win strategy, including cross-functional efforts to sharpen our prioritization of markets and channels.”
Mike Smith, President and CEO of Lamb Weston

articles.title: Levi Strauss: Q3 Revenue Rises 4% To $1.6 Billion As Company Raises 2026 EPS Outlook
articles.snippet:
Levi Strauss & Co. reported third-quarter net revenue of approximately $1.6 billion, up 4% on a reported basis and 5% organically.
The post Levi Strauss: Q3 Revenue Rises 4% To $1.6 Billion As Company Raises 2026 EPS Outlook appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Levi Strauss: Q3 Revenue Rises 4% To $1.6 Billion As Company Raises 2026 EPS Outlook
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Levi Strauss: Q3 Revenue Rises 4% To $1.6 Billion As Company Raises 2026 EPS Outlook
Levi Strauss & Co. reported third-quarter net revenue of approximately $1.6 billion, up 4% on a reported basis and 5% organically.
Operating margin was 13.8%, while adjusted EBIT margin reached 15.5%.
Diluted earnings per share from continuing operations were $0.43.
Adjusted diluted EPS reached $0.48.
Revenue in the Americas increased 4% on a reported basis and 2% organically, although U.S. revenue declined 1%.
European revenue increased 4% reported and 5% organically.
Asia revenue increased 5% reported and 10% organically.
Beyond Yoga revenue increased 9%.
Levi Strauss said its international and wholesale businesses delivered strong growth, while direct-to-consumer results were below internal expectations.
The company expects DTC revenue to return to mid-single-digit growth during the fourth quarter.
Management also elected to reinvest a majority of its tariff refund benefit into growth initiatives during the third and fourth quarters.
Levi Strauss plans to initiate a $100 million accelerated share repurchase program.
For fiscal 2026, the company now expects approximately 7% reported revenue growth and approximately 6% organic growth.
Adjusted EBIT margin is expected to expand to approximately 12.1%.
Adjusted diluted EPS guidance increased to $1.54 to $1.56 from the previous range of $1.46 to $1.52.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our third-quarter performance highlighted the power of our diversified portfolio and reinforced our confidence that we have the right strategies in place.”
Michelle Gass, President and CEO of Levi Strauss & Co.
“Reflecting confidence in our outlook, we are raising our full-year profit guidance and plan to initiate a $100 million accelerated share repurchase program.”
Harmit Singh, Chief Financial and Growth Officer of Levi Strauss & Co.
